summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and SummitGrid to explore resale/integration for GPU-backed private deployments. High interest in co-marketing and joint pilots; technical vetting needed for kernel/quantization compatibility and routing/prefix caching behavior.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (SummitGrid - Head Partnerships), Evan (SummitGrid - Cloud SA), Rafael (SummitGrid - BizDev)

[00:00] Lena: alright, hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood, i'll kick us off, um -- appreciate you carving out time. quick roundtable?
[00:10] Priya: hey lena, priya here. excited to talk, summit grid has been looking at a few partners to help with gpu hosting for our enterprise customers.
[00:20] Evan: evan, cloud solutions architect. i'll be the technical person on our side for integration questions.
[00:27] Rafael: rafael, biz dev, i'll be tracking commercial opportunities.
[00:31] Marcus: marcus here, se with redwood, i'll cover perf and deployment patterns.
[00:35] Lena: awesome; agenda, quick intros, partner model (resell vs integration), technical fit (private deploy / dedicated), compliance/enterprise asks, next steps. sound good?

[02:10] Marcus: quick context on redwood — we run a high throughput inference runtime, support hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments into vpc or on-prem. Our focus is production economics — latency, cost, reliability. sometimes i say red wood, sorry, 
[02:30] Evan: yeah we've seen you in a few benchmarks. curious about the dedicated offering — is that basically you'll host a pool we spin? or do we run the runtime in our infra?

[03:05] Marcus: good question. two patterns. for partner resell we can run dedicated pools in our infra with workload isolation and an sla. for a tighter integration or channel where you manage infra, we have a private deployment model — control plane can be customer-managed, we provide the runtime package and orchestration. both support k v cache, batching, quantization profiles.

[04:12] Priya: on the commercial front, we're mainly interested in being able to offer turnkey gpu clusters to our telco and finance customers with either co-managed or resale. key asks: sso/saml for auth, audit logs, and support for customer-managed kms.
[04:35] Lena: all standard asks — we have sso/saml, role-based access, audit trails, and kms integrations (HSM options) in private. we'll share SOC2 docs and our partner security page.

[06:00] Rafael: can you share the pricing model? our customers care about per-token inferences but also about sustained throughput pricing for fine-tuned models.
[06:20] Marcus: pricing depends — hosted usage is per-token, dedicated reserved capacity is commit-based monthly, private is typically an enterprise license + support. for pilot runs we can do short-term reserved capacity estimates. we'll follow up with a pricing matrix.

[08:00] Evan: technical — what GPUs / kernels do you support? specifically for Llama-family and some 8-bit quantized models, we need good perf on A100 and some newer H-series. also curious about kernel selection and if you support custom kernels for partner hardware.
[08:24] Marcus: we have tunings for A100, H100 and recent Ampere variants; we do kernel selection and compilation at deploy time, and we can tune for partner hardware. small caveat — if you're running very custom boards we may need a short engineering engagement. our runtime supports quantized formats commonly used, and we do continuous batching / prefix caching to save cost.

[10:30] Evan: are there any known issues with multi-tenant vpc networking or ipv6? some of our carriers enforce ipv6 and strict routing.
[10:45] Marcus: private deployments sit behind customer-managed networking so you control ipv6; for our hosted/dedicated pools we can enable vpc peering and private endpoints, but we'll need to map routing with your network team.

[13:10] Priya: on go-to-market, we see three modes: referral / reseller (you host), co-managed (we swap traffic to your runtime in our marketplace), or embedded (we ship your runtime as an offering in our console). which is easiest to start?
[13:34] Lena: reseller is fastest — we run the infra and you resell seats. co-managed needs some integration work but is good mid-term. embedded takes more product work.

[15:00] Marcus: some technical items to note for co-managed / private: model pinning and rollout controls, canary vs ab testing across model variants, and routing policies for latency vs cost. our runtime exposes metrics per-token and tracing hooks.

[17:10] Evan: good — for our pilots we want a way to pin a quantization profile per-customer and to have predictable tail latency SLOs. can you guarantee tail latency?
[17:28] Marcus: we work with SLAs for Dedicated; for private deployments measurables depend on customer infra but the runtime has knobs — batching windows, cache warmup strategies, and automatic fallback to CPU or smaller models. guarantees require capacity reservations.

[19:40] Rafael: do you integrate with third-party billing / marketplace APIs? we have a marketplace that handles entitlements.
[19:52] Lena: yes, we have marketplace integrations and can export usage/billing data; we also support token-level cost breakdowns.

[22:00] Priya: security — SOC2, ISO, we need to show customers we have audit logs and KMS. also, data residency in EU is important for a few customers. can you pin regions?
[22:20] Marcus: yes, region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private. hosted api we have regional endpoints in eu and na; private/on-prem meets residency needs. we'll share docs and SOC2/ISO evidence.

[25:00] Evan: long-term question — do you support custom operators / tensor cores for our Aurora boards? we might want very low-latency compiled paths.
[25:20] Marcus: we can explore kernel-level tuning; often it's a short eng project. we also maintain a model catalog with verified performance profiles for common models.

[29:00] Priya: what's needed from us to start a pilot?
[29:10] Lena: three things — a pilot use-case description, infra footprint (gpus, network), and a primary technical contact. we'll propose a pilot scope and a benchmark plan.

[31:00] Evan: on benchmarking, can you run a small throughput/latency run against our sample prompt set? we'd like to compare p95 latencies on H100 and A100 with 8-bit quantized configs.
[31:22] Marcus: yes, we'll run a benchmark. would prefer you send a sanitized prompt set and target sequences. we'll provide a spreadsheet of token counts, p50/p95/p99, and cost estimates.

[34:15] Rafael: marketing / co-selling — we can do a joint webinar and a one-pager. do you have partner marketing assets?
[34:30] Lena: yes, we have a partner playbook and slide deck. i'll send the partner deck and a one-pager, and we can coordinate a webinar.

[36:00] Priya: legal and contracting — we'll need an NDA and then a partner agreement draft.
[36:12] Lena: i'll loop legal, we'll share an NDA and standard reseller agreement.

[38:20] Evan: any gotchas with model weights and IP? some customers want us to ensure weights don't leave their environment.
[38:34] Marcus: if it's private/on-prem, weights never leave the customer's infra. for dedicated pools we have options for customer-managed keys and contractual controls. we'll capture requirements in the pilot scoping doc.

[41:00] Priya: sounds good. can we get a timeline for the pilot? 3-4 weeks for setup then a two-week benchmark?
[41:12] Marcus: that's reasonable. setup often 1-2 weeks for private deploys if infra is ready; benchmarks two weeks. we'll propose a plan once we see infra details.

[44:00] Lena: recap / next steps: Marcus will share integration spec, benchmark template and pricing matrix; Priya/Evan will send infra footprint and pilot use-case; Lena will introduce legal and share partner deck and SOC2 docs. schedule technical deep dive for next week.
[44:22] Priya: agreed. thanks all.
[44:30] Evan: thanks, bye.
[44:33] Rafael: bye.
